Comment 1 | created 2018-05-25T01:59:59Z
Source: https://github.com/OneSignal/OneSignal-WordPress-Plugin/issues/132#issuecomment-391918609
@stefa98 You will need to first disable automatic init the OneSignal WordPress does. 

1. At the bottom of the OneSignal WordPress settings you will need to toggle on "Disable OneSignal initialization".

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/645861/40521376-244a6a8a-5f80-11e8-9ab9-73eb786f0687.png)

2. Then you can initialize OneSignal through javascript with the `requiresUserPrivacyConsent` setting.

```html
<script src="https://cdn.onesignal.com/sdks/OneSignalSDK.js" async></script>
<script>
  var OneSignal = window.OneSignal || [];
  window._oneSignalInitOptions["requiresUserPrivacyConsent"] = true;
  OneSignal.push(["init", window._oneSignalInitOptions]);
</script>
```
`window._oneSignalInitOptions` contains all the settings from the WordPress plugin including app_id are already set in here.

3. When the user accepts your privacy agreement you will need to call `userTappedProvideConsentButton`
```javascript
function userTappedProvideConsentButton() {
  // Will initialize the SDK and register for push notifications
  OneSignal.push(function() {
    OneSignal.provideUserConsent(true);
  });
}
```

Issue body:
For us maintainers it's really hard to judge which features of the admin interface people are using/not using.

It'd be nice to add opt-out analytics where we can collect (anonymized, obviously) information about what people are doing with the Keystone admin interface so we can adapt to what users are actually doing!

_Yes I realize this isn't a bug, but this wouldn't make sense to be on Product Pains since it's mostly maintainer-facing_


Issue discussion:
Comment 1 | created 2016-06-24T17:58:59Z
Source: https://github.com/keystonejs/keystone-classic/issues/3075#issuecomment-228416235
Can we also use this thread for missing features?


Comment 2 | created 2016-06-24T20:21:32Z
Source: https://github.com/keystonejs/keystone-classic/issues/3075#issuecomment-228452450
No, this issue is specifically about introducing something like Google Analytics to the admin interface. Please submit individual issues to Github or feature requests to Product Pains!


Comment 3 | created 2016-06-25T10:29:13Z
Source: https://github.com/keystonejs/keystone-classic/issues/3075#issuecomment-228530152
Could this issue relate to the overall architecture of the project, and more specifically to the potential split between a "core" codebase and "plugins"?
What I mean by that is that if we had a "core" package, and then "plugin" packages, you would know which additional features are being used just by looking at the number of downloads / issues created / PR submitted for each individual plugin.
I feel that adding another feature to the project (this time, analytics) is not a good solution to help shipping v4... Instead, it should be the opposite, the codebase should be getting lighter.
It doesn't really make sense that there are so many issues related to Cloudinary and so on, when a lot of users will never use that service and are just waiting for a stable release of basic v4 (like me :) )
The example of babel and their strategy for going from v5 to v6 seems a good example, don't you think? They isolated a core and externalized a lot of plugins, and in the process had to design a clear API for each plugin to integrate with core. I would love to see that with Keystone as well.


Comment 4 | created 2016-06-25T10:57:38Z
Source: https://github.com/keystonejs/keystone-classic/issues/3075#issuecomment-228532266
> They isolated a core and externalized a lot of plugins, and in the process had to design a clear API for each plugin to integrate with core.

That's what we're working towards and is one of the big reasons v4 is such a long update! (sorry about that…)
We are now using react, which will very easily allow us to split out and integrate new fields (like Cloudinary), which in combination with #3052 will make our life maintaining the core a lot easier.

We will definitely not make that happen for v4, since we do want to get that released asap, but it's very very high up on our roadmap!

> I feel that adding another feature to the project (this time, analytics) is not a good solution to help shipping v4...

This is not a feature per-se, as no user will ever see this. This is solely for us maintainers, and it's very important and I do want to get this in before the v4 release.

We maintainers have no clue what the hell people are doing with Keystone, and while Product Pains was a good first step to get more clarity it's not enough. Adding analytics to the interface (which will hopefully will not be too difficult, shouldn't really delay the release anyway) will help us massively to focus on making those features that people are actually using better!

Comment 7 | created 2016-07-12T20:40:57Z
Source: https://github.com/keystonejs/keystone-classic/issues/3075#issuecomment-232173759
Big thumbs down from my end. Remember when [Strongloop tracked user version distribution by abusing npm](https://github.com/strongloop/loopback/issues/1079)? Granted, this planned tracking in Keystone is a very different (and less shady) scenario but please read those user's reactions to being tracked by OSS.

Do other popular npm modules engage in this kind of opt-out tracking? I expect this kind of thing from SaaS but **never** in OSS.

If you want usability feedback there are less underhanded and frankly **more effective** ways of getting this data, including compensated IRL usability trials & voluntary usability surveys.

This kind of tracking blurs the line between commercial product & OSS in a way that I am not comfortable with.

Comment 19 | created 2016-07-13T16:24:02Z
Source: https://github.com/keystonejs/keystone-classic/issues/3075#issuecomment-232408934
@morenoh149 those are features we don't have yet, not how our existing features are used.

To provide my perspective on why this is valuable, we currently have several APIs that integrate file uploading to S3 and Cloudinary integrated with TinyMCE. I'd _love_ to rip them out and make room for better ones based on the new Storage stuff that's in the works. The problem is I don't know whether there are 5 or 5000 people using those features.

Knowing what's being used, and how, is only going to become more important in terms of understanding which features are safe to deprecate, which to invest in, and whether we're actually optimising Keystone for its real audience. We only interact with a small fraction of users here and in other channels, in terms of total installs. Most of our usage is totally opaque.

These aren't questions that usability trials can answer for us.

re: Strongloop's blip - that's hostile because it was sneaky, you couldn't opt out of it, was a technical abuse of peer dependencies, exposed a vulnerability, and caused install delays / errors. I didn't see a lot of complaints that would be relevant given the way @mxstbr is designing this for Keystone.

In terms of whether there's a precedent for OSS to track usage, I think that's mixed. I mentioned Yeoman already. Node itself obviously doesn't/can't; npm tracks heaps of things. If you're serving something, nobody questions whether you can do analytics; if you're charging people, the same. We're disadvantaged because we're building software, not services, and giving it away under the most liberal license possible for free. Kind of ironic :)

Something I'm really interested in is whether django, wordpress, and other apps similar to Keystone do any of this (unfortunately a search for "Wordpress analytics" is pretty useless). Although I'm sure wordpress have a tonne of usage data just from wordpress.com which is completely controlled by Automattic.

@JedWatson

Issue body:
### Acknowledgements

- [X] I acknowledge that I have read the above items

### Describe the bug

LocalStorage of "greylisted" websites is not cleared at browser restart (and maybe also some other piece of data)
I detected the bug in particular with website https://www.lefigaro.fr/

The first time you access to this website, it asks for your consent to cookies, and records your answer, in order to do not ask you the same at your next access.
Your consent is not stored in a cookie (lefigaro.fr do not actually create any cookie) but in LocalStorage.

If there is no rule defined in CAD relative to this website, cleansing of this data (your consent) is correctlty done by CAD if you close the tab, a/o switch in the tab to another domain a/o restart the browser, and when the cleansing is done, re-opening the site asks again for your consent.

But if there is a "GreyList" rule defined on the domain, with all boxes checked ("Keep ... until restart"), the cleansing is not done if you "only" close the tab or switch to another domain (which is expected behaviour), but no cleansing as well is done EVEN IF YOU RESTART browser... whch is a bug.


### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce 

Step 1:
To start on a "blank page", clear in Firefox all data relative to any website.
Do not create any rule in CAD, neither Blank nor Grey, relative to lefigaro.fr
Suspend automatic cleansing in CAD
Open www.lefigaro.fr and give (or reject) your consent to cookies
Close the tab, or switch to another domain, or restart the browser
Open again www.lefigaro.fr and see that your consent is no more asked
Activate automatic cleansing in CAD
Close the tab (the one opend on lefigaro.fr), or switch to another domain, or restart the browser
Wait for automatic cleansing
Open again www.lefigaro.fr and see that now your consent is again asked.

Step 2 :
To start also this 2nd step on a "blank page", clear again in Firefox all data relative to any website.
Create in CAD a "GreyList" rule, on "*.lefigaro.fr", with all boxes ("keep until restart") checked.
Activate automatic cleansing in CAD
Open www.lefigaro.fr and give (or reject) your consent to cookies
Close the tab, or switch to another domain.
Open again www.lefigaro.fr and verify that your consent is no more asked (normal, since "GreyList")
Restart the browser
Wait for automatic cleansing
Open again www.lefigaro.fr and see that your consent is still no more asked.... while it should if cleansing at restart has been effective.


### Expected Behavior

To have ALL data relative to GreyListed website (including the LocaStorage) cleared at browser restart,and then to have the website asking again for your consent to cookies.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### System Info - Operating System (OS)

Windows 10 Pro 21H1

### System Info - Browser Info

Firefox 90.0.2 (64 bits)

### System Info - CookieAutoDelete Version

3.6.0

### Additional Context

_No response_

## Description

As an ecoverse host, I want to ensure that I am gdpr compliant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Investigate options for a react component that manages the user acceptance of cookie / tracking preferences
- [ ] Detail what we track on the client

## Additional Context

[GDPR Cookie compliance](https://gdpr.eu/cookies/#content:~:text=Cookie%20compliance,their%20consent%20in%20the%20first%20place.)

```
To comply with the regulations governing cookies under the GDPR and the ePrivacy Directive you must:

- Receive users’ consent before you use any cookies except strictly necessary cookies.
- Provide accurate and specific information about the data each cookie tracks and its purpose in plain language before consent is received.
- Document and store consent received from users.
- Allow users to access your service even if they refuse to allow the use of certain cookies
- Make it as easy for users to withdraw their consent as it was for them to give their consent in the first place.
```

# What data do we want?

Most data related with our audience/page view. For example,

- When do your users visit?
- Where are your users?
- What pages do your users visit?
- How are your active users trending over time?
- What are your top devices?

# Why do we need that data?

1. To provide numbers for funders
2. To assist when making decisions

# Why do we need to review it uses?

Although we collect the data, isn't clear who is the gate keeper for it. Most of the data that we collect with Google Analytics could make public and avoid maintainers and other volunteers to ask around how to access that data.

Comment 1 | created 2021-10-01T08:09:18Z
Source: https://github.com/carpentries/styles/issues/290#issuecomment-932016184
Note: I am not a lawyer, but this is my understanding of how this works.

## Possible violation of GDPR, without cookie banners

I see that this issue was created around the time GDPR was implemented in the EU and has not been discussed ever since. A caveat of using Google Analytics is that without _explicit user consent being requested via annoying cookie banners_ at every lesson, the Carpentries would be in _violation of GDPR._

## Alternatives exist

Open source solutions (such as Matomo and Plausible) which do not track personally identifiable information would 

1. be better suited for an organization of such standing
2. respect the user's privacy
3. have possiblity to self-host
4. not need cookie banners

- https://matomo.org/blog/2018/04/how-to-not-process-any-personal-data-with-matomo-and-what-it-means-for-you/

Issue body:
For some compliance frameworks you need to log users out automatically after a certain period of inactivity.

Notification polling kills our auto-logout: you never get more than 30 sec inactivity. It should be ignored when determining the inactive period of a user. Same with heartbeat and perhaps other things.

Comment 1 | created 2018-07-16T15:43:19Z
Source: https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues/7864#issuecomment-405291451
Session idle timeout is definitely an important factor when securing sensitive data - especially now when the new EU law on data protection and privacy has come into play.
We are hoping to start up with nextcloud this fall and are having some trouble as well with session lifetime. As jospoortvliet is mentioning, Nextcloud are having a notification pooling / heartbeat happening every 30 sec that possibly is keeping the session active even though the session are meant to expire. Practically when session lifetime is configured to 29 seconds in nextcloud's config.php file like this:

'remember_login_cookie_lifetime' => 0,
'session_lifetime' => 29,
'session_keepalive' => false

users are being logged out after 29 seconds. But when it is set to 30 or more - users are not being logged out.

This is, for us, a huge security concern when working around unauthorized people every minute of the day with laptops.

Issue body:
## Description

We added [GDPR Enforcement module](http://prebid.org/dev-docs/modules/gdprEnforcement.html) for TCF v2.0 recently. One of the features of this module states that, if a user doesn't consent to purpose 4, Prebid won't send userId data to the adapter. We request all the adapters listed here to use standard Prebid api/code when available and not add their own custom code to access user id. 
Purpose 4 implementation details are still in discussion and enforcement rules may change.

User Ids include - **user.buyeruid**, **user.id**, **user.ext.eids**, **user.ext.digitrust**  and **device.ifa**, **device.macsha1**, **device.macmd5**, **device.dpidsha1**, **device.dpidmd5**, **device.didsha1**, **device.didmd5**

Find more details about TCF enforcement [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBRaodKifv1pYsWY3ia-9K96VHUjd8kKvxZlOsozm8E/edit#heading=h.t62kkttx488d)

Prebid.js provides all configured userIds to adapters under the `bidRequest.userId` / `bidRequest.userIdAsEids` object. To enforce purpose 4, these two objects will not be passed to the adapters if consent is not given.

In light of this, all adapters will have to read user id information from either of the two objects mentioned above.

Few adapters have been found populating user id values from other sources. If you are a maintainer of any of the adapters listed below, please submit a PR in which you read the values from `bidRequest.userId` or `bidRequest.userIdsAsEids` object.

###### 1. user.buyeruid
- deepintentBidAdapter.js - Copies this value from `bid.params`. Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/deepintentBidAdapter.js#L122) line. @sourabhg
- luponmediaBidAdapter.js - Copies this value from `bidRequest.crumbs.pubcid`. Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/luponmediaBidAdapter.js#L200) line. @adxpremium @EfdalMustafic
- seedingAllianceBidAdapter.js - Copies this value from `bidRequest.crubms.pubcid`. Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/seedingAllianceBidAdapter.js#L130) line. @SeedingAllianceTech

###### 2. user.id

- deepintentBidAdapter.js - Copies this value from `bid.params`. Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/deepintentBidAdapter.js#L121) line. @sourabhg
- luponmediaBidAdapter.js - Generates a new id on the client side. Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/luponmediaBidAdapter.js#L196) line. @adxpremium @EfdalMustafic

###### 3. digitrust ID

I've few few bid adapters read the value of Digitrust ID from the window object. Should they not read it from `bidRequest[0].bidder[].userId.digitrust` ?

- gumgumBidAdapter.js - Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/gumgumBidAdapter.js#L95) line @mikewilso @jddeleon
- luponBidAdapter.js - Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/luponmediaBidAdapter.js#L322) line @adxpremium @EfdalMustafic
- pubmaticBidAdapter.js - Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/pubmaticBidAdapter.js#L596) line @pm-harshad-mane
- rubiconBidAdapter.js - Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/rubiconBidAdapter.js#L836) line @robertrmartinez
- sonobiBidAdapter.js - Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/sonobiBidAdapter.js#L342) line @JonGoSonobi
- prebidServerBidAdapter - Getting Digitrust Id from the config. Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/prebidServerBidAdapter/index.js#L249) line

###### 4. user.ext.eids

- prebidServerBidAdapter.js - Reads this value from `bids.0.userIdAsEids`. Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/prebidServerBidAdapter/index.js#L593) line

###### 5. user.ext.digitrust

 - Refer to **3 digitrust ID**

###### 6. device.ifa

- platformioBidAdapter.js - Reads this value from `bid[].params`. Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/platformioBidAdapter.js#L245) line @barslev @varashellov
- windtalkerBidAdapter.js - (Almost identical code to platformioBidAdapter.js) Reads this value from `bid[].params`. Check [this](https://github.com/prebid/Prebid.js/blob/3513d38c120072380c0f4a2376b95f50bb957224/modules/windtalkerBidAdapter.js#L245) line @barslev

Linked pages and attachments are not fetched. Issue body: *Updated March 21, 2018, to reflect latest plans for this feature's implementation:* MetaMask currently shows the selected account to each site that is visited. This is not an acceptable privacy feature, and user adoption has escalated the urgency of addressing this issue. It has also been also criticized that the `web3` API is visible at all, even to sites a user did not explicitly show it to, since this also provides some identifying information. ## Goals/Constraints - A user's accounts should never be shown to a site without the user's deliberate consent. - `web3` should not be exposed to sites by default. - Dapps should have a method of requesting a user's account & the web3 API. - Old Dapps should continue to work. ## Proposal: A PostMessage Based Log-In A difficult challenge of the constraints above is simultaneously *not* providing the `web3` API while also allowing sites to request a user to sign in. At first I thought this was impossible, but @kumavis, being the browser hacker he is, pointed out that as a WebExtension, we are able to listen to pages that use the [postMessage API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/postMessage), and so sites can send us a request without knowing whether we are listening or not. This flow would look something like this, from an internal `mural.ly` board: ![screen shot 2018-03-21 at 2 56 25 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/542863/37739669-2191c828-2d18-11e8-9ba1-6b0d23a1eaef.png) A design for this stage can be seen in #3383: ![deliberate log in flow](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/597770/37371849-07c77c62-26ce-11e8-9be9-cf6f79edb7f3.png) ## What Still Needs Defining: Message Format We need to define the exact format of the message sent via `postMessage`. To keep this format compatible with other web3 browsers, we could not require the `targetOrigin` property of that API, which restricts possible recipients. ### Constraints of the Message Format - Cannot use the `targetOrigin` API, to allow other web3 browsers to receive this event. (We're friendly!) - Should be unique enough to not accidentally interfere with other listeners (ideas?) - Should be extensible, to eventually include parameterized requirements of the Dapp (Need a certain network? Need a number of accounts? Need an account with a certain token? Maybe this becomes a way to add [DID](https://w3c-ccg.github.io/did-spec/) compliant personal information requests!) Related: #2532, #3663 and #3604 ## What Still Needs Defining: Design, Scope of Rollout In issue #3383 you can see initial designs, and how we're exploring what the UX of this type of log-in might look like. There are a variety of open questions there, asking whether we should rush out the privacy component (not showing web3 or accounts) if it means we remove the ability to be signed in to multiple sites at once. There are also several other UX/design concerns on that issue, and we can keep the design aspect of this feature mostly confined to #3383, and keep this issue for the specification of the API for Dapp developers. Maybe this becomes a way to add DID compliant personal information requests!)"_ Now that I looked into it more, my comment is probably better suited to https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-extension/issues/2532, the RFC where you discuss "Selective Disclosure" of personal info. So I am imagining flow is: user visits dApp, and dApp sends `postMessage` requesting a bunch of information, only *some* of which I am willing to share in order to use minimum feature set of dApp. Am imagining that instead of a binary `share account info / don't share account info` button there are some base settings associated with my account which excludes identifying information i dont want to share by default. Given the immense risk of someone's Ethereum account being compromised and the incredible number of attack surfaces a web-page/browser-extension/browser-code environment provides, perhaps it's time to think about some form of inter-app handshaking? I was wondering about something like this. It would require Metamask to host a server just to service the handshaking but it would be a lightweight server, probably with just a Redis cache to back it up. Here's what I was thinking: - The web page that's about to initiate a Metamask transaction creates a nonce to identify the new transaction, let's call it the _transaction nonce_, whose sole purpose is to provide a key for the MTCS to represent the current transaction. - It submits the _query nonce_ directly to the Metamask Transaction Control Server (MTCS for brevity's sake), waiting for a new nonce generated by the MTCS as a result of its query. This new nonce would be the _control nonce_. It uses an encrypted websocket connection to receive the response (to hide the transaction from other browser extensions that might be listening to post/xhr requests). - The web page notifies the Metamask extension of the payment request, providing the _query nonce_ sent to the MTCS. - Metamask contacts the MTCS with the _query nonce_ to get the _control nonce_ This simultaneously results in the MTCS server pushing the the _control nonce_ to the web page on its encrypted websocket connection. - The web page then asks Metamask to trigger the usual SEND/REJECT dialogue to confirm the transaction, providing the _control nonce_ it received from the MTCS - Metamask checks the _control nonce_ received from the web page to make sure it matches the one it got directly from the MTCS server earlier. If not, it returns an error and does not show the SEND/REJECT dialogue. Otherwise, execution proceeds at normal. By having this parallel level of communication over encrypted web sockets between the web page and the Metamask extension, with the MTCS trusted server in the middle, I believe it would create a protocol layer that locks out other browser extensions and domains from snooping in on the transaction and thereby creating havoc. What do you think? results.rationale: MetaMask 原先把选中账户注入每个站点，并使 web3 对任何页面可见，作者认定这是不可接受的隐私问题，提出目标：未获用户主动同意不得向站点显示账户、默认不暴露 web3、Dapp 仍能请求登录、旧 Dapp 仍可用。方案是站点发 postMessage 请求，扩展监听后提示登录（不能用 targetOrigin，否则别的 web3 浏览器收不到）。评论指出消息格式若过于复杂（网络、账户数、代币、DID 属性等参数），在用户同意场景下反而可组合出指纹，建议移到选择性披露的 RFC。MTCS 握手提案被判与本议题无关。2019 年以 connect screen 上线（#4703/#3930）为完成标志关闭。

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
To comply to the GDPR regulation about:
Right of withdrawal ('the right to be forgotten'): request its deletion when the data is no longer necessary.

We need to manage that data without delete user, to avoid possible problematic records about mandatory relationships, airline stats, etc.
I am not sure if this already works like this. In any case, it could be useful if a pilot wants to go back and recover all his progress after asking for his data to be deleted.

Currently when we change the user's state to "deleted" both their name and email remain in the system.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
By changing the state of the pilot to "deleted" the system could overwrite his name in the database to something like john doe, or take just the first letters, his initials, "JDD" (John Doe Doe) of his full name.
For email I don't know what would be the perfect solution. ¿And password?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Comment 4 | created 2022-10-25T16:52:13Z
Source: https://github.com/phpvms/phpvms/issues/1490#issuecomment-1290860750
"_Soft delete always_" ? I do not think that is needed, even with GDPR. 

Technically for GDPR compatibility a user can request data removal and our current system covers regulation requirements pretty well;

1. User has "non personal data" (pireps, acars records, finance records etc) in the system : 
   *Remove personal data (change name, mail, password, ivao/vatsim id etc) , make non personal data non-identifiable / trackable*
2. User has NO "non personal data" in the system : 
    *Delete the user directly*

For scenario 2 we do not need to "soft delete", we just need to delete the record that's it.

In short, **just click the delete button from admin area** v7 will take care the rest.
(_or if needed we can allow the users to delete themselves from user profile directly_)

So again, I really and honestly do not understand the feature request or the logic behind it. @arv187 is technically requesting the same thing we already have but wants it to have with more clicks ? Either he is unaware of the current system or wanting something different like;

`... In any case, it could be useful if a pilot wants to go back and recover all his progress after asking for his data to be deleted.`

Second part of this request is not possible and should not be possible. 

Once you request a GDPR removal **there is no way of going back** . It is a removal decision and it is a serious act, not something you change two days later. So if the person wants to join back he/she needs to start from the beginning like every other **new member**.

Hello @jackjackde and thank you for using our module and submitting an issue.

The tracker does two things : 

- it collects data through a local domain (you are the only one having access to this data) about customer navigation (product view, bought, facet usage, etc...). This part is meant to be used later on our roadmap to build behavioral optimizers (boost most viewed products and things like this).

- it sends a ping to a smile domain, with the url of the website using elasticsuite. Nothing more. It is just a way for us to track the module usage. Since it's published free and does not require any subscription or account anywhere to use it, it's a way for us to have statistics about the number of websites the module is deployed on.

I hope to have answered your question. Do not hesitate if you want to know more.

Released issue metadata:
Issue title: Update EE6 to remove all persistent cookies in default state
Project: ExpressionEngine/ExpressionEngine
Issue type: issue
Matched keywords: "['cookie law']"
GitHub labels: ["enhancement: accepted"]
Status in release: closed
Comments in release: 2; discussants: 2
Reported: 2021-03-23 18:56:58+00; last active: 2021-06-03 12:58:18+00
Issue number: 955

Supplemental evidence: complete | comments retrieved 2/2
Scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.

Issue body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
EE mostly uses session based cookies, but sets a number of "Strictly Necessary" cookies that are "persistent" beyond the session.  These are flash (1 day), last_activity (1 year), last_visit (1 year), remember (2 weeks),  visitor_consents (1 year).

The presence of these persistent cookies trips a wire in GDPR - for each of these cookies it is necessary for the developer to provide justification for the need for the persistent cookie and report that the cookie cannot be linked to user activity.  Sometimes these justifications are not heard sympathetically - if the 'strictly necessary' determination is not accepted then these cookies must only be set if a visitor to the site from a GDPR country actively consents.

There is no mechanism in EE either to adjust the duration of these cookies, or to link their creation to active consent.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An option in EE CP to set the duration of all cookies to be session based by default.

If there are functional benefits to be gained by making any of the cookies have a longer life, this should be a choice that can be made by users and set using the consent features of EE.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There are no alternative solutions right now.

**Teachability, Documentation, Adoption, Migration Strategy**
How this gets documented depends on the solution that is adopted.
Provided switching to session duration cookies is not something that breaks EE, there should be no migration issues.


Issue discussion:
Comment 1 | created 2021-03-24T20:14:42Z
Source: https://github.com/ExpressionEngine/ExpressionEngine/issues/955#issuecomment-806157312
Yes the cookie issue is becoming more and more important in meeting various laws across the globe. More and more governments are introducing privacy/cookie laws of various strengths so we need the ability to be able to micro manage all EE cookies to meet requirements.

Ideally a fresh EE install wouldn't set any cookies by default (aside from CP related cookies which fall under strictly necessary), we'd then be able to enable them as needed with parameters as JCogs suggests, either via the Consent module or implied consent (which can sometimes be fine). 

We need to stay as current as possible with laws. If EE doesn't adapt here it could soon prevent new developers coming on board?

Comment 2 | created 2021-03-25T01:34:19Z
Source: https://github.com/ExpressionEngine/ExpressionEngine/issues/955#issuecomment-806293981
building on @blue-dreamer comment there may be a case for EE to put itself at the extreme end of the compliance spectrum since it seems different countries enforce privacy regulations differently - discussion in Slack suggests that GDPR in Belgium and Germany is more stringently enforced than in UK - e.g. apparently logs of all consent decisions (even ones where consent is anonymously declined) are required. Not sure how we find / define the boundary conditions, but probably makes sense for an assumption of 'implement the more private case as a default' and 'keep better logs' options should be general principles to inform decisions.

results.rationale: 提案指出 EE 主要用会话 cookie，但仍会设置若干跨会话的持久 cookie（flash 1 天、last_activity 1 年、last_visit 1 年、remember 2 周、visitor_consents 1 年），而系统既不能调整其期限，也不能把其创建绑定到主动同意；若“严格必要”的认定不被接受，这些 cookie 就必须先获同意。诉求是控制面板提供“默认全部改为会话 cookie”，确需长期保留的由用户选择并经同意模块启用。评论支持并主张全新安装默认不设非必要 cookie，同时按更严格法域（如比、德要求记录同意决定）取最保守默认。议题被标为 accepted，但无实现证据。

Issue body:
#### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Visit this page: https://jetpack.com/support/for-your-privacy-policy/
2. Uncheck everything but Sharing
3. See copy text.

#### What I expected

Info about the the request to Facebook, LinkedIn or Pinterest (for example) to get the sharing count information.

#### What happened instead

> Sharing
> Data Used: When sharing content via email (this option is only available if Akismet is active on the site), the following information is used: sharing party’s name and email address (if the user is logged in, this information will be pulled directly from their account), IP address (for spam checking), user agent (for spam checking), and email body/content. This content will be sent to Akismet (also owned by Automattic) so that a spam check can be performed. Additionally, if reCAPTCHA (by Google) is enabled by the site owner, the sharing party’s IP address will be shared with that service. You can find Google’s privacy policy here.

This text does not mention any requests to Facebook et al. for getting the counts.

This need to get mentioned for GDPR compliance and maybe there could be an easier way to opt out than using a filter: https://jetpack.com/2016/04/15/hook-month-customizing-sharing/

Source: https://github.com/WICG/ua-client-hints/issues/132#issuecomment-717193684
A lot has happened since these experimental ideas were first proposed earlier in 2020. The UK’s CMA have recommended common personal identifiers as a remedy for competition issues in the [digital online marketplace](https://www.gov.uk/cma-cases/online-platforms-and-digital-advertising-market-study#final-report). Such identifiers will have a significant impact on all proposals and work with privacy as justification. Given this proposal seems to be at least in part solving a problem related to privacy the proposal will be impacted and should be aligned to this broader requirement.

The report recognizes the need to maintain existing use cases and features until alternatives are found that create a level playing field. As such this proposal is dependent on defining alternative solutions for all the use cases listed.

Regulators including the European Commission have identified dominant vertically integrated market participants maintain their dominance by capturing agreement for all products and services at the point of accepting consent for an essential service. Therefore, a dominant player may obtain consent and access to information that is practically denied to their competitors.

The TPAC session this afternoon might be an opportunity to discuss this in more detail.

Issue body:
I'm not trying to open old wounds, but we're currently discussing whether or not we need some sort of cookie banner in our pretix solutions (both self-hosted and cloud-based).

https://github.com/pretix/pretix/issues/95 states that we don't need to inform users about cookies in pretix. If we still use only the cookies mentioned in that issue we're home safe according to https://www.iubenda.com/en/help/5525-cookies-gdpr-requirements#exemptions (we have a “[Privacy](https://pretix.eu/about/en/privacy)” link on all shop pages; cf. https://pretix.eu/ulf-test/8/privacy/, say).

Can anybody (more versed in both pretix and the cookie law than me) confirm that we still use only the cookies mentioned in https://github.com/pretix/pretix/issues/95 and that having the Privacy link on all shop pages makes pretix comply with the current EU cookie law?

Best regards,
Mikkel



Issue discussion:
Comment 1 | created 2020-08-20T08:09:53Z
Source: https://github.com/pretix/pretix/issues/1752#issuecomment-677448059
We're no lawyers and EU cookie law is confusing and contradictory.

We believe that the cookies set by pretix (as long as you do not use something like the pretix-tracking or pretix-campaigns plugin) are only used for purposes that can be considered essential for technical purposes (carts, logins, security, language). pretix (by default) does not use cookies for any kind of tracking or profiling purposes, so you should be fine.

That said, we *do* plan to add more advanced cookie consent management to pretix at some point, we just haven't got around to it yet and we don't think it's really necessary.

Comment 2 | created 2020-08-20T09:30:20Z
Source: https://github.com/pretix/pretix/issues/1752#issuecomment-677488617

Issue body:
We use membership across all the Joystream pallets to reflect user activity and maintain their reputation. The current implementation of the referendum is more abstract and doesn't require membership for usage. We could integrate the referendum pallet with the membership pallet.

#### Pros
- a consistent approach for the pallets - we use membership everywhere without any exceptions
- user reputation benefits from voting 
#### Cons
- lack of privacy 
- more complex solution
- additional dependency for the pallet

Issue discussion:
Comment 1 | created 2021-01-06T13:37:08Z
Source: https://github.com/Joystream/joystream/issues/1986#issuecomment-755302657
The lack of privacy may not be a problem there. As long as the membership can be bought, a user wanting maximum privacy can acquire voting currency from an exchange or privacy-focused tool (like Coinjoin, Tornado cash, etc.), buy a membership, and vote privately. This brings only one extra step (buying membership) in comparison to a referendum without membership.

If we ever want to provide truly anonymous elections, we need to upgrade the voting mechanism with some Zero-Knowledge proofs or similar technology.

Using `--dnssleep 120` is the way and only way to disable doh checks.

We need to know how long we have to wait before we can continue to get the cert.

Issue body:
Hello we are building a bot where we get personally identifiable information from the user. Hence we need to make sure that this data is not saved in any way on any Microsoft database. Hence We are currently building our own BotState (StateApi) to connect our personal DB instead of the default Azure one available out of the box.

When we connect to our Bot using Direct Line Apis using the following steps:

1) The DirectLineApi posts message to the bot using  userConversations.PostMessage(conversationId, msg)
    ----> This hits our custom BotState source code as expected.

2) But when we call userConversations.GetMessages(conversationId), --> It does not seem to invoke our BotState code. But the messages have appeared on the client side.

3) We also tried closing down this connection and tried to call the userConversations.GetMessages(conversationId) after 2 minutes. It again seem to have not invoked our code, but have the messages appear to the user.

This gives us a feeling our messages are further stored somewhere in Hub (probably directline.botframework.com?) which is a concern for us. Could someone please throw some light on if and how the messages are stored in the hub inspite of us overriding the BotState?

Also how does watermark work when the BotState does not seem to have anything to do with watermarks.
userConversations.GetMessages(conversationId, waterWark.ToString());

Issue discussion:
Comment 1 | created 2016-11-03T21:59:44Z
Source: https://github.com/microsoft/botframework-sdk/issues/1580#issuecomment-258287082
Currently the bot state api is only used to store internal tracking information for the BOT itself. 

DirectLine is a channel and it uses azure table storage with the data encrypted to provide clients ability to get the state of a conversation.  It does not use the bot state api.  Allowing it to have a conversation storage API is good idea and we will add to our enhancement list.


Comment 2 | created 2016-11-03T22:12:23Z
Source: https://github.com/microsoft/botframework-sdk/issues/1580#issuecomment-258289918
Thanks for your reply. Do we know how long would that data in azure be stored (Also which DataCenter)? Is there a chance we can dictate the datacenter that this storage can take place in the future for legal reasons? Also Does that mean other channels also use their own table storage? 


Comment 3 | created 2016-11-05T15:10:54Z
Source: https://github.com/microsoft/botframework-sdk/issues/1580#issuecomment-258617693
No, all of the other channels are able to pass their data through, they act as a proxy which takes care of transport and translation but no storage.  The DirectLine channel on the other hand is acting as a store and forward service, aka, you have a mobile app which is started up and connects to a conversation to get the latest messages from the conversation.  This requires the data to be stored in an intermediate server awaiting a client to ask for it.

We are looking at ways that we can have directline store the data in dev controlled location, but as of now we don't support it.

I believe we store the data encrypted in our storage layer, and I don't know what the expiration but I know the data does expire (I think it is 7 days)


Comment 4 | created 2016-11-06T17:39:55Z
Source: https://github.com/microsoft/botframework-sdk/issues/1580#issuecomment-258696703
Data retention in Direct Line is 24 hours although we've had many requests to shorten/eliminate this, and we're considering it for our backlog.

## Alternatives

Released issue metadata:
Issue title: Add description on what cookies are used and what they do
Project: ActiveLogin/ActiveLogin.Authentication
Issue type: issue
Matched keywords: "['cookie law']"
GitHub labels: ["enhancement", "BankID", "GrandID"]
Status in release: closed
Comments in release: 2; discussants: 2
Reported: 2019-11-09 14:13:38+00; last active: 2019-11-12 20:04:06+00
Issue number: 156

Supplemental evidence: complete | comments retrieved 2/2
Scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.

Issue body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In EU, "[the cookie law](https://www.cookielaw.org/the-cookie-law/)" requires you to show info on what cookies you store and for what reason. We lack such documentation today and it makes it difficult to explain to the end user what cookies we store and for what reason.

**What area is it related to**
This relates to the packages that might store cookies, and they are:

- `ActiveLogin.Authentication.BankId.AspNetCore`
- `ActiveLogin.Authentication.GrandId.AspNetCore`

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Write documentation on the cookies used in `Readme.md`, and also a short notice in code.

**Additional context**
In Active Login the only cookie we store, is a cookie containing the `AuthenticationProperties`, containing things like `RedirectUri`. But `AuthenticationProperties` also has a property bag where the user can set their own things, so could contain any kind of data depending on how it's used.

The `AuthenticationProperties` is set in the consuming code when doing the challenge, and a sample can be found in [AccountController.cs](https://github.com/ActiveLogin/ActiveLogin.Authentication/blob/master/samples/IdentityServer.ServerSample/Controllers/AccountController.cs#L42-L55):

```csharp
public IActionResult ExternalLogin(string provider, string returnUrl)
{
    var props = new AuthenticationProperties
    {
        RedirectUri = Url.Action(nameof(ExternalLoginCallback)),
        Items =
        {
            {"returnUrl", returnUrl},
            {"scheme", provider}
        }
    };

    return Challenge(props, provider);
}
```

We have followed the convention that Microsoft uses themselves, and stores the `AuthenticationProperties` in a state cookie. The name of them are by default this, but can be overridden.

- `__ActiveLogin.BankIdState`
- `__ActiveLogin.GrandIdState`

Look at (for example) the [implementation for Twitter auth](https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/master/src/Security/Authentication/Twitter/src/TwitterHandler.cs#L141-L158) done by Microsoft to see where we got our inspiration. There seems to be little or no documentation on the exact approach here, only source code.

Note, in addition ASP.NET Core Auth might issue cookies themselves, depending on how you configure your pipeline. But that's outside the scope of Active Login.

Issue discussion:
Comment 1 | created 2019-11-09T20:09:41Z
Source: https://github.com/ActiveLogin/ActiveLogin.Authentication/issues/156#issuecomment-552133029
I’m not an expert on the cookie law, or how we use them in this library, but do we not fall under this category (my emphasis):

Examples of cookies that generally do NOT require consent:
- User input cookies, for the duration of a session
- **Authentication cookies, for the duration of a session**
- User-centric security cookies, used to detect authentication abuses and linked to the functionality explicitly requested by the user, for a limited persistent duration
- Multimedia content player session cookies, such as flash player cookies, for the duration of a session
- Load balancing session cookies and other technical cookies, for the duration of session
- User interface customisation cookies, for a browser session or a few hours, when additional information in a prominent location is provided (e.g. “uses cookies” written next to the customisation feature)

From: https://wikis.ec.europa.eu/display/WEBGUIDE/04.+Cookies

If the user chooses to use AuthenticationProperties to store sensitive data, then they are the ones that need to deal with the cookie law I would assume?

Maybe it’s good practice to implement this anyway, but I am not sure we have to. How are similar libraries dealing with this, e.g. IdentityServer?

Comment 2 | created 2019-11-09T22:40:26Z
Source: https://github.com/ActiveLogin/ActiveLogin.Authentication/issues/156#issuecomment-552144221
Great finding @viktorvan!

The intention was not to display any message to the user, rather explain what our cookies do for developers, so they can decide whether or not they need to tell the users about it.

We had a developer asking about this info.

Very good that auth cookies seems to be an exception to the EU thing.

**What do you think about an auto-delete function, which removes posts that are older than n days / months / years?**

* Users would be given more control over their privacy. Even if users post in public - opinions and attitudes change and sometimes we wish we hadn't said or written something months or years ago. This is no perfect mechanism, but what if we were able to just let Mastodon "forget" the past?

Issue body:
This feature issue is based on a discussion in issue #2304 
>> Another problem in context of this topic is that (to my understanding) only people with "editing" permissions are allowed to investigate the audit trail.

>Indeed it is true. I wasn't really aware of this and will make the necessary changes so it can be accessed in view mode, too.

As it turns out, the access to the audit trail is very broad and more fine control is needed. According to GDPR regulations, it must be possible to delete GDPR related data from electronic systems like elabFTW. In contrast to be compliant with FDA's "21 CFR part 11"  an audit trail recording all changes is needed. Both statements are somewhat exclusive to my opinion. The only solution I see is that access to an audit trail can be narrowed down to very limited number of people, at least for some specific experiment. 
@NicolasCARPi  Do you have any more ideas?

Ideally, access settings for audit trail can be also enforced by admins to ensure that the system configurations are compliant as stated above.


Issue discussion:
Comment 1 | created 2022-07-25T21:12:18Z
Source: https://github.com/elabftw/elabftw/issues/3731#issuecomment-1194635933
I think it really depends on the contract signed between the employee and the company. The lab notebook is generally the property of the employer. The purpose of the GDPR law is to inform the user why their data is stored, with whom it is shared and for how long it is stored and what is stored. If it is clear from the beginning that the name of the person **needs** to appear for at least 10 years next to their results from the start, I think it's okay. It just needs to be written in the contract. This is an HR problem.

> According to GDPR regulations, it must be possible to delete GDPR related data from electronic systems like elabFTW

~~~mysql
update users set firstname = 'redacted', lastname = 'redacted', email = redacted@gdpr.eu where userid = N;
~~~

Now it's anonymous. It can be as simple as that. But will the name be erased from the timestamped pdfs? No. Would it be reallistically possible to have 100% anonymization for a user without defeating the whole purpose of the app? Probably not.

Again, I've already spent a bit of time reading about GDPR over the years, and I'm pretty sure the main point is to **inform** the user and ask them for **consent** (which they can revoke). If it is clear that it is not revokable, it is IMHO fine, as long as the user knows about it.

There are some ELN companies out there that are perfectly happy selling your personal data to marketing companies outside the EU, and they tell you about it in their privacy policy, which you agree one when using their platform. And they say "we are fully GDPR compliant".

eLab is already very good on that side, being an open source tool with strictly no external information leakage. When you use the self-hosted eLab you don't have a third party that needs to comply. It becomes "you", the company, that has a contract with the employee.

So for me we are very far from news website tracking you on the web and selling your data to marketing companies for targeted advertising without your knowledge or consent, which is the target of this regulation.

Anyway, not a simple matter for sure....

Comment 2 | created 2022-07-25T21:50:24Z
Source: https://github.com/elabftw/elabftw/issues/3731#issuecomment-1194675536
Hi Nicolas,
Thank for the detailed answer. Unfortunately, it seems it did not make myself very clear. My concerns were not related to the user of elabFTW. I am pretty sure their data are very well protected (we have it in our hands ;-) ) and there should not be any GDPR related risks. 

I was more addressing another use case:
We are generating and processing lot's of GDP related data during our experiments and thus to make fully use of an ELN from time to time it would be good to mention within some experiment descriptions some data which fall under GDPR regulations. E.g. mentioning some blood parameters or clinical variables and linking it to a patient ID already falls under GDPR regulations (we have discussed those topics in long with external auditors, consultants and customers). According to 
"Art. 17 GDPR Right to erasure (‘right to be forgotten’)" there must be an opportunity to delete such entries or at least fully anonymize them i.e. remove ids.  This is especially critical for data within the scope of  "Special category of data".

Of course those entries can not be removed from audit trails and and also not from time-stamped pdfs. So both should fall under special "permission settings" which allow to fine control access.
I know it is a tedious and laborious topic but I am sure it will become more and more important in future. So might be better to think of it in time?   We already have such discussions with our auditors and customers as mentioned above and need to make sure to comply.  
 



 

Comment 3 | created 2022-07-25T21:55:53Z
Source: https://github.com/elabftw/elabftw/issues/3731#issuecomment-1194680481
In my opinion, the data should be pseudonimized before reaching the lab, so before reaching the lab notebook. The lab notebook should only ever see "Patient X23B" and never "Bill Gates's blood".

So the way I see it you need to have a process **before** it reaches the lab. And you'll only have a single point where the correspondance between the ID and the real name exists and it's easy to delete from there. This way you avoid errors, impossibilities and remove the possibility for lab workers to even see the personal data in the first place!

Comment 4 | created 2022-07-25T22:04:58Z
Source: https://github.com/elabftw/elabftw/issues/3731#issuecomment-1194688678
> In my opinion, the data should be pseudonimized before reaching the lab, so before reaching the lab notebook. The lab notebook should only ever see "Patient X23B" and never "Bill Gates's blood".
> 
> So the way I see it you need to have a process **before** it reaches the lab. And you'll only have a single point where the correspondence between the ID and the real name exists and it's easy to delete from there. This way you avoid errors, impossibilities and remove the possibility for lab workers to even see the personal data in the first place!

Yes,  and that's of course a process we have in place. But errors can still happen (and unfortunately live is sometimes not that easy) so I thought it would be good to have some kind of a "second option" if data are entered by mistake.  

Comment 5 | created 2022-07-26T10:30:30Z
Source: https://github.com/elabftw/elabftw/issues/3731#issuecomment-1195305089
Generally I think @NicolasCARPi  ist right. Just because someone requests deletion does not mean that data really needs to be deleted. If there is a legal obligation (like 10 years data storage retention for a laboratory accreditation) you do not have to remove that data. See also https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/law-topic/data-protection/reform/rules-business-and-organisations/dealing-citizens/do-we-always-have-delete-personal-data-if-person-asks_en

Then again, this is really a question for a lawyer. Nothing that IT can answer. What could be the middle ground is data locking. I think that is also what @manuSrep proposes. A separate status or special tag for an experiment so that when set only an auditor can still view it. Or so that reading is logged and an explanation why needs to be given.

PS: In general I would rather not store a patient id or name in elabFTW but link the experiment url in your patient file. Because generally I think - maybe I am wrong for your usecase - the scientist in the lab will only process the sample but does not need patient data for that. So he or she should not ever see that data. Even a ID number is personally identifiable information.

Issue body:
**Don't shoot please.**
  
I think it would be useful for the project if we knew how many people use the clients on what OS.  
This could be further expanded by adding specific counters to each function.  
  
This way:  
- We would know if a version becomes depreciated. For example, Windows XP 32-bit. Is it still very popular? Or maybe just 5 person uses it all over the world?  
- Does anyone use the most advanced torrent sorting functions, or it's just that one John Doe who made a ticket for it?  
  
And so on. Just two ideas. 
**All the stats would be anonymous of course, and public. Since the client is public, anyone could check the code themselves. The code would ping back to our server, and not to anyone else. Only the most crucial data would be sent back, and we would never publish the entire dataset in raw form.**
The main benefit of doing this would be that people would have global numbers (tell me you don't like numbers) and the project team would know what features do people even use. Like if there is a feature that requires extensive work, but it's barely used if ever, then it could be removed/phased out.  
  
Again, just an idea, thanks for reading it.  
  
Common arguments:  
- What if the NSA hacks the server and steals the data and then they beam up my pets?!  
As I wrote above only the most crucial things would get sent and they would be made public anyhow. Like no one cares how many times you opened the RSS reader for example, and since the data sent would be anonymous, it's also worthless. No, no code would be added to track what things you search for.   
  
How could it be implemented?  
Well, I am no telemetry magician. The client would simply call the server in some way. Some secure way, so the data could not be tampered with (i.e.: no 12 year old could just ruin the dataset). Also, we could count installations simply, or request a Windows computer name, ID, whatever, then compare if it's been reported in the past few months, and so on. It's quite extensive what you can do, but the main thing is that the feature should be useful and harm no privacy.

> All the stats would be anonymous of course

I see this was opened pre-GDPR, so consider this:

There is no such thing as anonymous when you are receiving the IP address of the sender. Considering that according to GDPR the IP address is personal data and any processing of personal data must be based on:

- informed choice
- freely given (not forced) consent

any such option should:

1. Be OFF by default (= it should be an **opt-in**, not an opt out)
2. Inform the user of the consequences of its enabling (for him, not for the data controller)
3. Give him an option to still be able to use the program without opting in.

> Don't shoot please.

Too late. You have been shot :P

If one chooses FOSS one chooses its for the freedom it gives. Usually telemetry and stats are aimed to optimize a product/service commercially, i.e. it benefits a centralized entity.

results.rationale: qBittorrent 用户提议加入功能使用计数遥测：统计各 OS/版本的安装量、各功能使用频次，用于判断哪些功能可下线。提案强调只回传最关键数据、数据公开、代码可审计。评论指出开源项目无法做到防伪造遥测，任何校验和或加密都无效；有人认为采集机器名或 MAC 地址侵入性过强（提议者回应只是组合用于“签名”，并承认可能过头），并提出可由每个安装生成 installation UUID。随后有 GDPR 评论指出：只要收到发送者 IP 就不存在“匿名”，IP 属个人数据，因此遥测必须默认关闭（opt-in 而非 opt-out）、须告知启用后果、并保证不启用仍可正常使用程序。2022 年维护者以“不计划实现”关闭议题，并说明 Fosshub 下载统计已能提供各 OS 用户比例这类基础数据。全程无实现或合并证据。
results.scope_note: 提案未采纳（维护者以“不计划”关闭，以 Fosshub 下载统计替代）

Issue body:
- WordPress 4.9.6
- WP Rocket 3.0.5-beta1
- EU Cookie Law 3.0.1

EU Cookie Law set up with default settings, only checked the _Activate_ option.

Cookie message gets added on the front-end; **should go away after a click on the _Ok_ button, but doesn’t.**

Activating the _Auto Block_ option in EU Cookie Law fixes the issue. However, since we say WP Rocket supports this third-party plugin, we should fix this on our end.

Issue discussion:

Source: https://github.com/wp-media/wp-rocket/issues/1010#issuecomment-393824779
Apparently, it’s not always the _Auto Block_ option only. User feedback:

> With just _Auto Block_ enabled, the problem persists. 
> However, when I check _Excluded scripts(/beta)_, the banner disappears on click.

_[(ticket reference)](https://secure.helpscout.net/conversation/591613128/70010?folderId=714999)_

Comment 2 | created 2022-01-20T23:00:49Z
Source: https://github.com/wp-media/wp-rocket/issues/1010#issuecomment-1018001523
Tested with `EU Cookie Law 3.1.6` and WP Rocket 3.10.6, the message goes away correctly.

results.rationale: 环境为 WordPress 4.9.6 + WP Rocket 3.0.5-beta1 + EU Cookie Law 3.0.1，仅勾选 Activate。现象是提示条在前端出现，点击 Ok 后不消失，即同意动作未被持久化、横幅持续拦截。报告者说启用 EU Cookie Law 的 Auto Block 后问题消失，但因官方声明支持该第三方插件，仍应在本插件侧修复。评论补充 Auto Block 并非稳定有效：有用户仅启用 Auto Block 时问题依旧，只有勾选 Excluded scripts(/beta) 后点击才消失，说明不同设置路径下表现不一致。2022 年用 EU Cookie Law 3.1.6 + WP Rocket 3.10.6 复测，提示条可正常消失，属新版组合下的自然恢复，但未给出代码级根因或修复提交。
results.scope_note: 新版组合复测恢复（根因与修复提交未定位）

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Mozilla partenered with Cloudflare for their DoH resolver and they have a resolver (https://mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query) which limits logged data and data retention, opposed to the 1.1.1.1

Comment 1 | created 2018-10-27T16:12:31Z
Source: https://github.com/bromite/bromite/issues/164#issuecomment-433633656
This is the special agreement: https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/commitment-to-privacy/privacy-policy/firefox/

The privacy policy for 1.1.1.1 is instead: https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/commitment-to-privacy/privacy-policy/privacy-policy/

In both cases you can see:
> All information collected by Cloudflare, no matter whether such information is part of Cloudflare’s temporary or permanent logs, will be cleansed of any personally identifiable data (including your IP addresses). Additionally information that is stored as part of Cloudflare’s permanent logs will be further anonymized.

An important question: is the main difference between the two that Cloudflare is sharing this DNS data with Mozilla? It is not stated explicitly that it is not the case.

The only difference I can see is that the data used for Cloudflare permanent logs contains less fields, but I would like to know if there is an agreement between Cloudflare and Mozilla about sharing such data first.

**Edit:** I think the wording gives away the relationship between Cloudflare and Mozilla:
> Any data Cloudflare handles as a result of its resolver for Firefox is as a date [sic] processor acting pursuant to Firefox’s data processing instructions.

(date is a typo, should be data)

This means Firefox (they mean Mozilla?) is the data controller second GDPR parlance, thus it also has access to the data.

If this is the case, then I deny this request: we do not need to share the data with two companies instead of one.

Issue body:
The *get started* page of flutter.dev says:

>  The flutter tool uses Google Analytics to anonymously report feature usage statistics and basic crash reports. [...]
> To disable reporting, type `flutter config --no-analytics`. [...]
> If you opt out of analytics, an opt-out event is sent, and then no further information is sent by the Flutter tool.

According to the [GDPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Data_Protection_Regulation "GDPR = General Data Protection Regulation") and a recent German court decision, analytics are defined as non-necessary services and require explicit, voluntary consent before *flutter* can send any data. Providing a CLI flag or a first-run opt-out is illegal in the EU/EEC.

:pray: Please, make `fluter` never send an opt-out event when the user opts out of analytics.
:pray: Please disable analytics by default. You may fix that by adding a CLI flag:

    flutter config --enable-analytics

:pray: Please, Alphabet employees, respect the law, don't be evil.

* 2020-03-10 [Google Remains Atop List of GDPR Fines](https://www.datanami.com/2020/03/10/busted-google-remains-atop-list-of-gdpr-fines/)
* 2020-03-11 [Sweden fines Google $8 million for right-to-be-forgotten violations](https://venturebeat.com/2020/03/11/sweden-fines-google-8-million-for-right-to-be-forgotten-violations-and-demands-it-keep-websites-in-the-dark/)
* 2020-06-19 [French court slaps down Google's appeal against $57M GDPR fine](https://uk.news.yahoo.com/french-court-slaps-down-googles-170442213.html)
* 2020-07-14 [Google’s failure to respect the « right to be forgotten » results in €600,000 fine](http://lawrope.com/googles-failure-to-respect-the-right-to-be-forgotten-results-in-e600000-fine/)
* 2020-12-10 [France fines Google $120M and Amazon $42M for dropping tracking cookies without consent](https://uk.news.yahoo.com/france-fines-google-120m-amazon-085553384.html)

User privacy matters, please better respect them.

Source: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/73657#issuecomment-757541171
Hi @iapicca and Happy New Year

Thank you for reading this request carefully.

For clarification:
1. By default, Flutter enables analytics
2. GDPR defines analytics as not necessary, so analytics require explicit, voluntary consent before any data is sent.
3. Therefore, to comply with GDPR, Flutter shall disable analytics by default.

Also, if the user disables analytics, Flutter shall not send any analytics => Flutter shall not say *"Hey, there is one flutter here, but analytics is disabled"* every time the configuration is reset (multiple times when running in a fresh container).

I am sorry that I only listed articles about web/OS. My intention was to show that GDPR is serious (mandatory since 2018), but it seems to be hard to comply with for some companies.

VSCode has the same issue, and I should create a similar issue for VSCode.
But I do not care much about VSCode, because I am happy to use [VSCodium](https://vscodium.com/) instead.
I highly recommend you to use VSCodium. :+1: VSCodium is free as in freedom. VSCode is not open source. I also recommend you [ungoogled-chromium](https://ungoogled-software.github.io/) in lieu of Google Chrome. For example, ungoogled-chromium respects the system's DNS settings (Chrome bypasses the system's DNS settings, maybe that changed recently, not sure). Google Chrome is not FLOSS.

I appreciate how Google helps FLOSS projects, I love what you guys at Google do for the open source community, but I do not want to be tracked by Google products anymore. I think more and more Flutter developers consider the user privacy. I would like to see the Flutter developers agree for voluntary consent before sending any data.

When I first start Firefox, a small banner allows me to explicitly enable analytics and automatic crash reporting. I voluntary enable it because I want to help the Firefox project, and because I appreciate having control over what goes out from my personal computer.

To better respect user privacy (and GDPR), we could implement something similar to the following idea:
1. Keep flag `--no-analytics`.
2. Add flag `--enable-analytics` to allow users to explicitly consent.
3. If neither flag `--no-analytics` nor `--enable-analytics`, and no configuration, Flutter asks:
    > Enable analytics and automatic crash reporting in configuration?
4. Flutter never sends any data to remote servers if analytics is disabled.

Issue body:
Hello Joomla-Community,

Data protection law has been in force in Europe since 2018.

A handful of GDPR plugins were programmed for Joomla. But only one on the market, which you also have to buy, has observed all legal points.

As an IT expert, I simply do not understand why a cookie banner has not been implemented in Joomla or in other CMS for a long time.

It is important that a website visitor has to agree before loading scripts or fonts from other websites. Likewise, not a single cookie may be set before consent has been given.

The law also says that cookies must be described to the website visitor. Name, purpose, duration, ...

In addition, a website visitor must be able to withdraw their consent at any time.

For this reason I am requesting this feature. It's been almost 5 years and neither in Joomla nor in other CMS was something integrated. It's the law. So it should be anchored at the core of every CMS.

BTW this is the only plugin which provide all the right functions for Joomla:
https://extensions.joomla.org/extension/gdpr/

The other plugins are just wrong for the EU. This can get very, very expensive if a law agent contact you, because some Google Fonts get downloaded or a Cookie get setted without a permission of the user.

Thank you in advance!

Best regards
Pascal

Issue body:
Currently, a local account can be linked with a federated account via the dashboard without actually having access to that federated account.

This can cause issues if the user misspells, or otherwise incorrectly enters, their federated account name.  A user should be required to prove that they have access to both accounts before they can be linked (similarly to the way linking a local account already requires the other account's password).

The most serious intentional misuse of this function I can think of offhand is to self-register a bunch of accounts and then link them all to another user's federated account, which could cause confusion for that user.  I haven't thoroughly explored how permissions might be shared with federated accounts at this point, but that could certainly be an area of concern as well.

Issue discussion:
Comment 1 | created 2018-04-16T16:44:04Z
Source: https://github.com/wso2/product-is/issues/2206#issuecomment-381670474
a possible more-aggressive misuse of this for spearphishing, under the assumption that IS is being used as an authN/Z layer for something allowing private details to be added:

1. malicious user (M) knows target user (T)'s name as provided by an external SSO identity provider (X).  I'll assume T has not yet used the system protected by IS, but has used X before
2. M links an account they control in IS to T's account in X
3. T logs in via X, thinking someone (their admin / service provider / automatic provisioning) had set up the account link for them
4. T enters private information (SSN, HIPAA/GDPR-protected info, etc)
5. M now has access to this information

Preventing step 2 in this chain would be the purpose of this request - I would argue it to be a relatively serious security hole.

Issue title: Enhancement: Allow adding organization-specific SQL rules using a plugin layer.
Project: sqlfluff/sqlfluff
Issue type: issue

Status in release: closed

Reported: 2020-02-05 13:35:29+00; last active: 2021-02-23 09:04:45+00
Issue number: 164

Supplemental evidence: complete | comments retrieved 9/9
Scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.

Issue body:
At Mailchimp, we have certain tables that contain sensitive information. In order to access this information safely, we have a few options:
* Instead of accessing the table directly, use a predefined view that filters out sensitive information
* If using the table directly, use a recommended set of filters, e.g. 

```
WHERE
  LOWER(TRIM(email)) NOT IN (
  SELECT
    email
  FROM
    opted_out_emails)
```

Initially, I think we'd simply check each query individually. In that case, I think it'd be great if we were able to implement these checks as classes similar to those in `src/sqlfluff/rules`. I was thinking a plug-in architecture could be good for this.

Farther in the future, I could imagine doing more sophisticated analysis, such as looking across queries (either CTEs within a single query, or separate queries). In this case, I'm not sure how that would work, but perhaps we'd want to just use SQLFluff as a library, not using the command line. There is _potentially_ a tool idea there as well -- having a tool to output the parse tree in a neutral format like JSON, etc.

Issue discussion:
Comment 1 | created 2020-02-09T20:50:25Z
Source: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/164#issuecomment-583891675
Well *that* is a very interesting idea! I'd not thought that far out.

Outputting the query as parsed JSON wouldn't be too hard - but I'm more curious about importing sqlfluff as a library and then extending it. Have you got any more detailed ideas about what that might look like?

Comment 2 | created 2020-02-09T21:04:37Z
Source: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/164#issuecomment-583893112
I think the ideal case is to define SQLFluff as a plugin host, similar to the recent work I did on `diff-quality`. Then other packages could register themselves as defining SQLFluff plugins. Then SQLFluff could easily "discover" those packages and import them. Given the way rules are defined with a decorator, e.g.:

```
@std_rule_set.register
class Rule_L001(BaseCrawler):
```

I think simply having SQLFluff import those libraries would be enough to incorporate them into the list of checks. There might be some additional considerations to make sure the class names or other identifying information doesn't "collide" with built-in checks. But overall, I think it wouldn't be that big of a change.

I only thought of this idea recently when someone on our Security team was looking at some of our queries and asked, did you remember to use "safe" table X rather than unsafe table Y. This could be a common type of requirements at other companies, and being able to handle this would add a lot of value to the tool. General code quality is nice, but security and confidentiality are very important.

Source: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/164#issuecomment-584300563
@alanmcruickshank: If it would be helpful in clarifying the proposed approach, I'd be happy to spend a few hours creating a proof of concept. The amount of code and work will be small enough that if it looks like a bad idea, we can replan in another direction.

FWIW, the `pluggy` package I used in `diff-quality` was "spun out" of the popular PyTest test framework. I have used it on two projects now, and I think it's some pretty elegant "glue". 😄

Source: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/164#issuecomment-718827299
Totally agree.
Plugins are a great feature for this kind of project. Because every organization has an additional set of checks.
Do you have a timeline for when are you going to release it?


Comment 6 | created 2020-10-29T20:00:50Z
Source: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/164#issuecomment-718988018
@valerii-vorobiov In theory the _beta_ version of organization rules is now possible. Check out #514 which added functionality for users to add their own custom rules, using the `sqlfluff` crawler. 

Do you think something like this meets your needs?

Comment 7 | created 2020-11-26T14:09:59Z
Source: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/164#issuecomment-734318946
This is not going to be part of the 0.4.0 release which should happen in the next few weeks.

This *is* however going to be one of the next big features I'd like to tackle. If people are happy to share, I'd love to have some examples here of the kinds of things that we'd like to do with plugins so that we have some easy targets to start with.

Comment 8 | created 2020-11-30T17:39:22Z
Source: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/164#issuecomment-735934888
Possible use cases for our organization:
* On BigQuery, we prefer `USING` over `JOIN` for brevity and readability reasons, in spite of the general recommendation adopted for SQLFluff core, so we'd flag places where it could be used.
* For privacy reasons, queries should avoid using certain of our internal tables, preferring related views that have been "cleaned" of users who have "opted out" from a GDPR/privacy perspective. If they do access these tables, they must `JOIN` with other tables to "manually" apply these filters.
* (This one is still vague) If the result of a query reads from tables known to contain PII (personally identifiable information), it **must** retain the specific fields (e.g. `user_id`) that allow the output data to be tied back to the source. Maintaining this "lineage" / backtracking info is critical in order to allow this data to later be scanned, filtered, and purged of information for users who have said "stop using my data for machine learning projects". This is a legal requirement for ours and many other businesses.
* If a query accesses an "external" table (i.e. from another GCP "project"), that table reference must be "frozen" to a particular date and time using the BigQuery `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF` syntax. This policy assures that query results are reproducible even if the underlying table data changes
  * backfills
  * a job for day X runs on day X+1 due to lag
  * a job fails and is retried

These are the ideas that are "top of mind". If it'd be helpful, I could take a closer look at some of our projects for other possible ideas. 

Comment 9 | created 2020-12-16T00:20:51Z
Source: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/164#issuecomment-745670108
Another use case: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/pull/514#issuecomment-745636097

Issue title: Anonymization script: scramble evaluation results
Project: e-valuation/EvaP

Status in release: closed
